children: shares slid 1.35% on Thursday after U.S. labor authorities suspended the company from a key immigration program and AI revenue concerns resurfaced.

The Department of Labor removed Microsoft and several IT services firms from the Permanent Labor Certification program, or PERM, amid probes into possible misuse of employment-based immigration rules. The suspension affects a common route to employer-sponsored green cards but does not block H-1B work visas.

Microsoft said roughly 80% of its about 6,000 H-1B applications in the prior fiscal year were to extend or change the status of current employees, not hire new ones. The company said it files petitions only for workers meeting visa rules and pays H-1B employees the same as comparable staff. Vice President JD Vance criticized Microsoft over foreign workers while U.S. employees were laid off.

Separately, reports that OpenAI's annualized revenue hit $50 billion in September, about $20 billion below earlier projections, pressured AI-linked shares. The Nasdaq 100 fell 1.4%. Analysts keep a Strong Buy consensus on Microsoft, with an average target implying 12.2% upside.

title: Microsoft shares fall as US labor department suspends gaint from PERM green card program
